q: In a broadcast hash join of a huge `orders` table with a small `products` table, what happens to the rows of `orders`?
o: They are shuffled by `product_id`
They are collected on the driver
They stay in their partitions and probe a local copy of the hash table
They are broadcast to every executor
e: Only the small side moves: it is collected, broadcast and built into a hash table on each executor. The big side is streamed in place.

q: What does `BuildRight` in a `BroadcastHashJoin` node mean?
o: The right side of the join was turned into the in-memory hash table
The right side was shuffled
The join result is written to the right table
The right side is the probe side
e: The build side is the one broadcast and hashed. `BuildRight` means the right-hand input became the hash table.

q: In `orders LEFT JOIN products`, which side can Spark broadcast?
o: Only `orders`
Either side
Neither side
Only `products`
e: The left side must keep its unmatched rows, so it has to be the probe side. Only the right side can be the build side.

q: With no hint, when does Spark plan a broadcast hash join at planning time?
o: When the join key is a string
When the estimated size of one side is below `spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold`
Always, for every equi-join
Only when the cluster has more than 10 executors
e: The optimizer compares size estimates with the threshold (10 MB by default in Apache Spark). AQE can also switch to a broadcast at runtime when a side turns out small.

q: A join that used to take minutes now fails with out-of-memory errors during a `BroadcastExchange`. What is the most likely cause?
o: The big side has too many partitions
The table needs `OPTIMIZE`
The broadcast side has grown, or stale statistics make it look small, so Spark copies a large table to every executor
Photon does not support joins
e: Every executor must hold the whole build side. Remove old broadcast hints and refresh statistics with `ANALYZE TABLE ... COMPUTE STATISTICS`.
